name: Self-Portrait
howTo: Open your Chess.com profile settings and upload any photo or avatar image — it just has to be a real picture, not the default silhouette.

name: Say Hello
description: Send a private message to another member.
howTo: Open any player's profile and use the message icon to send them a short note — a game request or a GG after a match both count.

name: Happy Anniversary
description: Reach one year since creating your account, and every year after.
howTo: Nothing to do but keep your account active — this fires automatically on each anniversary of your join date, shown on your profile.

name: Chess.com Supporter
howTo: Upgrade to any paid membership tier (Gold, Platinum, or Diamond) from the Go Premium page — any tier triggers this one.

name: Gift Wrap
description: Give someone else a Chess.com membership.
howTo: From another player's profile or the Gift Membership page, buy them a membership directly — a nice way to introduce a friend to the site.

name: Man Vs Machine
description: Play a game against a bot in Live Chess.
howTo: Open the New Game menu, choose Play a Bot, and pick any personality and difficulty — even a single move against the easiest bot counts.

name: Puzzle Newbie
howTo: Head to Puzzles from the main menu and solve any daily or rated tactics puzzle to completion — one correct solve is all it takes.

name: Puzzle Beginner
howTo: Work through the Puzzles trainer a few minutes a day; tactics improve fastest with short, frequent sessions rather than long cram sessions.

name: Puzzle Ace
howTo: Make puzzles part of your warm-up routine before rated games — pattern recognition built here transfers directly into spotting tactics over the board.

name: Puzzle Veteran
howTo: At this volume, review the puzzles you got wrong rather than just grinding forward — recurring themes (pins, forks, back-rank) are worth drilling specifically.

name: Puzzle Addict
howTo: Sustained puzzle volume like this is best built with a daily streak habit — even 5 puzzles a day adds up to thousands over a year.

name: Puzzle Machine
description: Solve 100 puzzles in a single day.
howTo: Set aside a dedicated block of time and work through puzzles back-to-back; skip puzzles you're stuck on rather than burning minutes on one, to keep the count moving.

name: Good Habit
description: Solve at least one puzzle on 7 days in a row.
howTo: Set a daily reminder or bookmark the Puzzles page — a short streak like this is about consistency, not difficulty, so even one easy puzzle a day keeps it alive.

name: Hot Streak
description: Solve 10 puzzles correctly in a row without using a hint.
howTo: Drop down to an easier puzzle rating temporarily if you're chasing this — a clean streak is easier to build at a level just below your normal rating.

name: Puzzle Battle
description: Play a Puzzle Battle against another member.
howTo: From the Puzzles menu, start a Puzzle Battle and invite a friend or an open opponent — whoever solves puzzles correctly fastest wins the head-to-head race.

name: Speed Solver
description: Solve at least 10 puzzles in a 3-minute Puzzle Rush.
howTo: In 3-Minute Puzzle Rush, favor speed over perfection on easy puzzles — a wrong answer costs one life, so keep moving unless you're genuinely unsure.

name: Rush Streak
description: Solve 5 puzzles in a row correctly during a Puzzle Rush run.
howTo: Warm up with a few untimed puzzles first so your pattern recognition is sharp before you start the Rush clock — cold starts are where early streaks break.

name: Train Your Brain
howTo: Drills are found in the Puzzles or Lessons area — start any drill set and make your first attempt at a position to unlock this.

name: Brains of Steel
howTo: Work through a variety of drill categories (endgames, tactics, checkmates) rather than repeating one — variety builds more transferable pattern recognition.

name: Silicon Brain
howTo: This is a completionist achievement — check the Drills section for any categories you haven't tried yet and work through the full list.

name: Surprise
description: Play your first game of Crazyhouse.
howTo: Crazyhouse lets you drop captured pieces back onto the board — from New Game, pick Variants > Crazyhouse and play one game to unlock this.

name: Mad Scientist
howTo: Crazyhouse rewards holding captured material for a well-timed drop near the enemy king rather than spending pieces the moment you get them.

name: Easy as 1-2-3
description: Play your first game of Three-Check.
howTo: In Three-Check, three checks against your opponent wins the game outright — from New Game pick Variants > Three-Check and play one game.

name: Three Strikes
howTo: Prioritize forcing checks even at a small material cost in Three-Check — a single check is often worth more than winning a pawn.

name: Higher Ground
description: Play your first game of King of the Hill.
howTo: King of the Hill is won by marching your own king to one of the four center squares — from New Game pick Variants > King of the Hill.

name: Mountain Climber
description: Play 10 games of King of the Hill.
howTo: Clear a safe path toward d4/d5/e4/e5 early and don't be afraid to walk your king up the board the moment it's safe to do so.

name: Worker Bee
description: Play your first game of Bughouse.
howTo: Bughouse is a team variant played on two boards where captured pieces pass to your partner — join or start a Bughouse game from New Game > Variants.

name: Hive Mind
howTo: Coordinate piece requests with your partner constantly — telling them what you need (or don't need) matters more than your own board tactics.

name: Random Thoughts
description: Play your first game of Chess960 (Fischer Random).
howTo: Chess960 randomizes the back-rank setup each game — from New Game pick Variants > Chess960 and play through one to unlock this.

name: Mix Master
howTo: Spend the opening moves establishing king safety and piece coordination before committing to a plan — the memorized theory you rely on elsewhere won't apply.

name: Dangerous Intersection
description: Play your first game of 4-Player Chess.
howTo: 4-Player Chess is played on a cross-shaped board with four players — find it under Variants in the New Game menu and join a game.

name: Battle Royale
howTo: Alliances shift fast in 4-Player Chess — watch which of the other three players is winning and don't hesitate to team up against the leader.

name: Second Opinion
description: Analyze a completed game with the game review tool.
howTo: Open any finished game and click Game Review or Analysis — reviewing your own losses for the critical mistake is the single highest-leverage study habit.

name: Hindsight 20/20
howTo: Build analysis into your routine right after you finish playing, while the position and your thinking during the game are still fresh in memory.

name: Statistician
description: Visit and review your own Stats page.
howTo: Your Stats page (under your profile) breaks down rating history, win rates by time class, and opening performance — worth a regular check-in.

name: Introspection
description: Use the My Games database to look further than 5 moves into a game.
howTo: The My Games archive lets you search your own history by opening and result — dig past the opening moves to see how your middlegames typically go wrong.

name: Contender
howTo: Browse the Tournaments tab for an open arena or swiss event in your time control and register — most run continuously so you can jump in immediately.

name: Competitor
howTo: Regular tournaments are one of the best ways to get long, focused practice at your time control against a stream of different opponents.

name: Challenger
howTo: At this volume, be selective about format — daily tournaments let you study each move without a clock, while live arenas build faster decision-making.

name: Organizer
howTo: From the Tournaments page, click Create a Tournament and configure the format, time control, and entry rules, then open it for players to join.

name: Director
howTo: Running recurring tournaments for a club or group of friends is the easiest way to rack this one up organically.

name: Club Member
howTo: Search Clubs for a community around your favorite opening, country, or interest, and hit Join — clubs also run their own internal tournaments.

name: Pack Leader
description: Create a club that reaches 10 members.
howTo: Create a club from the Clubs page, then invite friends or post about it in forums and your own games to attract members.

name: Team Player
howTo: Join a club that runs Team Matches, then sign up for a board when the next match opens — team matches pit clubs against each other over multiple boards.

name: Team Pillar
howTo: Being reliably available when your club's team matches open is what builds this up — check your club's events tab regularly.

name: Ballot Box
description: Play a game of Vote Chess.
howTo: Vote Chess lets an entire team decide each move by voting — join an open Vote Chess game from the Vote Chess section and cast a vote on any move.

name: Killer Pawn
howTo: Pawn mates usually happen when a pawn advances or captures onto a square next to a king that has no escape squares — look for these in cramped endgames.

name: Killer Knight
howTo: Knight mates need the enemy king boxed in by its own pieces — smothered mates on f7/f2 after a queen sacrifice that forces a rook to block are the classic pattern.

name: Killer Bishop
howTo: Bishop mates usually come on a long diagonal once the king is pinned to the back rank by your own or the opponent's pieces — clear the diagonal and look for it.

name: Killer Rook
howTo: The back-rank mate is the most common rook mate — a rook lands on the back rank while the enemy king is boxed in by its own pawns with no escape square.

name: Killer Queen
howTo: The most common mate in chess — queen mates usually follow when the queen is supported by another piece next to the enemy king. Nearly every won game ends this way.

name: Buddy System
howTo: Send friend requests from opponents' profiles after games you enjoyed — a quick GG message plus a friend request is a natural combination.

name: Social Butterfly
howTo: Club activity and tournaments are the fastest way to meet enough regular opponents to build a large friends list organically.

name: Bring a Friend
howTo: Use the Invite Friends option in your account menu to send an invite link, or just share your referral link directly with someone who plays chess.

name: People Person
howTo: Share your invite link in places chess players already gather — school clubs, local meetups, or group chats with friends who play casually.

name: World Traveller
howTo: Play at odd hours or in open live pools rather than only against friends — the matchmaking queue naturally pairs you with a wider spread of countries.

name: Pen Pal
description: Become friends with people from 10 different countries.
howTo: After a good game against someone clearly based elsewhere (check their profile flag), send a friend request — over time this builds a genuinely international friends list.

name: VIP Referrer
description: Have someone you invited upgrade to a paid membership.
howTo: This one depends on the person you invite finding enough value to upgrade themselves — introducing a serious improver to lessons and puzzles helps.

name: Front Page
howTo: Open the Articles/News section from the main menu and read any single article — game recaps, strategy pieces, and site news all count.

name: Reading Glasses
howTo: Chess.com's news coverage of top-level tournaments is a good habit-builder — following an ongoing event naturally racks up several reads a week.

name: Library Card
howTo: At this volume, subscribing to a specific beat (openings theory, endgame studies, or tournament coverage) keeps the reading useful rather than just a number to hit.

name: 1st Lesson
howTo: Open the Lessons tab and pick any topic that matches your current level — finishing one full lesson unlocks this.

name: "New" Complete
description: Complete every lesson in the New Lessons category.
howTo: Work through the New Lessons category from the Lessons tab in order — these are usually short, so a full sweep is a reasonable single sitting or two.

name: "Beginner" Complete
description: Complete every lesson in the Beginner category.
howTo: The Beginner track covers piece movement, basic tactics, and checkmate patterns — a solid foundation worth finishing even if you already know some of it.

name: "Intermediate" Complete
description: Complete every lesson in the Intermediate category.
howTo: Intermediate lessons focus on tactical motifs and positional ideas — pair them with puzzles on the same theme to cement what you learn.

name: "Advanced" Complete
description: Complete every lesson in the Advanced category.
howTo: Advanced lessons dig into deeper strategic and endgame concepts — take these slowly and replay the example positions on a board rather than just watching.

name: TV Guide
howTo: Open ChessTV from the main menu and tune into any live broadcast — a top-level tournament stream or a titled player's stream both count.

name: Couch Potato
howTo: Leaving a major tournament broadcast running in the background while you study or play adds up toward this quickly during big events.

name: TV Junkie
howTo: Marquee events like the Candidates or a World Championship match are the easiest way to accumulate large amounts of broadcast time.

name: Press Play
howTo: Video lessons sit alongside the interactive Lessons tab — open one and watch it through to unlock this.

name: Popcorn Lover
howTo: Mix video lessons with interactive ones — watching a concept explained, then immediately drilling it in an interactive lesson, reinforces it better than either alone.

name: Film Buff
howTo: At this point, focus your video watching on your actual weaknesses (check your Stats page for where you lose the most rating) rather than random browsing.

name: Movie Star
howTo: This is a heavy completionist achievement — treat it as a long-term side goal alongside your regular play rather than something to binge in one sitting.

name: 1st Word
description: Earn your first Chess.com activity point.
howTo: Activity points come from almost any interaction on the site — posting, commenting, or completing a lesson — so this usually unlocks itself quickly.

name: First!
description: Post the first comment on a Daily Puzzle.
howTo: Daily Puzzle comments reset each day — check the Daily Puzzle early after it refreshes and post a comment before anyone else does.

name: Participant
howTo: Regular engagement — playing, posting, and completing lessons — builds activity points passively as a side effect of normal site use.

name: Megaphone
howTo: Being active in forums and clubs, not just playing games, is usually what pushes activity point totals up fastest.

name: Chatterbox
howTo: This is a long-run accumulation — consistent, varied site activity over months is the realistic path here rather than any single burst of activity.

name: Conversation Starter
howTo: Head to the Forums section, pick a relevant category, and click New Topic — ask a real question or share an interesting game to get replies.

name: Soapbox
howTo: Use the Blog feature from your profile to write a post — a game analysis, an opening you've been studying, or a tournament recap are all good starting topics.

name: Printing Press
howTo: A regular series — like a weekly game-of-the-week writeup — is an easier way to reach 10 posts than trying to write one long one.

name: Giver
description: Give a trophy to another member.
howTo: Trophies are given from a player's profile page — after a good game or a helpful forum post, visit their profile and award one.

name: Awarder
howTo: Make a habit of trophying opponents after especially good or hard-fought games — it's a small gesture that also builds this achievement.

name: Generous Spirit
howTo: Active club members are a good source of opponents worth trophying regularly, since you'll play many of them repeatedly.

name: Trophy Hunter
howTo: Playing sportingly and being active in clubs and tournaments naturally earns trophies from opponents who appreciated the game.

name: Award Magnet
howTo: High-volume tournament and club play is the realistic path here — the more opponents you interact with, the more chances to be trophied.

name: Prize Winner
howTo: This tracks cumulative trophies received — regular, sportsmanlike play across games, clubs, and tournaments builds it up over time.

name: Wood League
description: Reach the Wood League tier in Chess.com's weekly Player Leagues.
howTo: Player Leagues rank you by weekly rating-points earned against similarly-ranked opponents — play consistently through the week and win more than you lose to climb into the Wood tier.

name: Stone League
description: Reach the Stone League tier in Chess.com's weekly Player Leagues.
howTo: Player Leagues rank you by weekly rating-points earned against similarly-ranked opponents — play consistently through the week and win more than you lose to climb into the Stone tier.

description: Reach the Bronze League tier in Chess.com's weekly Player Leagues.
howTo: Player Leagues rank you by weekly rating-points earned against similarly-ranked opponents — play consistently through the week and win more than you lose to climb into the Bronze tier.

description: Reach the Silver League tier in Chess.com's weekly Player Leagues.
howTo: Player Leagues rank you by weekly rating-points earned against similarly-ranked opponents — play consistently through the week and win more than you lose to climb into the Silver tier.

description: Reach the Crystal League tier in Chess.com's weekly Player Leagues.
howTo: Player Leagues rank you by weekly rating-points earned against similarly-ranked opponents — play consistently through the week and win more than you lose to climb into the Crystal tier.

name: Elite League
description: Reach the Elite League tier in Chess.com's weekly Player Leagues.
howTo: Player Leagues rank you by weekly rating-points earned against similarly-ranked opponents — play consistently through the week and win more than you lose to climb into the Elite tier.

name: Champion League
description: Reach the Champion League tier in Chess.com's weekly Player Leagues.
howTo: Player Leagues rank you by weekly rating-points earned against similarly-ranked opponents — play consistently through the week and win more than you lose to climb into the Champion tier.

name: Legend League
description: Reach the Legend League tier in Chess.com's weekly Player Leagues.
howTo: Player Leagues rank you by weekly rating-points earned against similarly-ranked opponents — play consistently through the week and win more than you lose to climb into the Legend tier.

name: Go Mobile (Android)
description: Play a game using the Chess.com Android app.
howTo: Install the Chess.com app from the Google Play Store, sign in with your existing account, and play a single game to unlock this.

name: Go Mobile (iOS)
description: Play a game using the Chess.com iOS app.
howTo: Install the Chess.com app from the App Store, sign in with your existing account, and play a single game to unlock this.

name: Tweet!
howTo: After finishing a game, use the Share option on the game page and post it to Twitter/X — a fun way to show off a nice win or a wild finish.

name: Like!
howTo: After finishing a game, use the Share option on the game page and post it to Facebook.

name: Friend Me
description: Connect your Facebook account to Chess.com.
howTo: In Account Settings, link your Facebook account — this can also make it easier for real-life friends to find you on the site.

name: Devoted
description: Log in for 7 days in a row.
howTo: A daily puzzle or a single quick game is enough to keep a login streak alive without needing a long session every day.

name: Fanatic
description: Log in for 30 days in a row.
howTo: Anchor your login to an existing daily habit — checking the Daily Puzzle each morning is a reliable way to sustain a month-long streak.

name: Survey Says
howTo: Site surveys occasionally appear as banners or in the News section — respond to one the next time it's posted to unlock this.

name: 3D Glasses
description: Switch your board pieces to 3D mode.
howTo: In Board & Pieces settings, toggle the piece style to 3D — a purely cosmetic change that unlocks this achievement immediately.

name: Finger Paint
description: Change your board or piece theme.
howTo: In Board & Pieces settings, pick any board color scheme or piece set different from the default to trigger this.

name: Eye Doctor
description: Play a game with a vision-accessibility setting enabled.
howTo: In Accessibility or Board settings, enable a vision-assist option such as colorblind-friendly highlighting or large pieces, then play a game.

name: Quick Knockout
description: Win a game in a small number of moves.
howTo: Fast wins come from punishing opening mistakes directly — memorize a few sharp traps in your main openings and watch for opponents who miss basic threats early.
